name: ClippingCandidateFinder
src_typeComment: The detection half of the Level Transform Guidance, and deliberately the DUMB half: a cheap, over-inclusive proximity test rather than exact penetration math. Its only job is deciding which objects get the highlight — the shader then shows the actual truth and a person judges intent, which is the one thing no amount of geometry math can determine.  That trade is what makes this work on mixed greybox + final-art levels at all: Physics.ComputePenetration (the exact option) doesn't support non-convex MeshColliders, which is exactly what stairs/architecture usually are. An over-inclusive bounds test works against ANY collider type, and a false positive costs nothing — the object gets highlighted, shows no red, and you move on.

src_members.comment: overlapTolerance SHRINKS the tested bounds before querying, which is what keeps normal resting contact out of the results: a crate sitting correctly on a floor touches it exactly, so a shrunk box no longer reaches it, while a crate genuinely sunk deeper than the tolerance still overlaps. That one knob is the difference between a useful list and a list containing every prop in the level.
